name: SQL Injection Prevention
description: Enforces parameterized queries and safe database access patterns to prevent SQL injection attacks.
content:
# SQL Injection Prevention Rules

- Always use parameterized queries or prepared statements — never concatenate user input into SQL strings
- Use your ORM's query builder — ActiveRecord, Prisma, SQLAlchemy, Eloquent all generate safe parameterized queries
- When writing raw SQL, use placeholders — `WHERE id = ?` or `WHERE id = $1`, never `WHERE id = '${id}'`
- Validate and type-cast input before it reaches the database layer — an integer ID should be parsed as an integer
- Use stored procedures with parameterized inputs for complex queries — but don't build dynamic SQL inside procedures
- Apply the principle of least privilege — database users should only have SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE on tables they need
- Never use database admin credentials in application connection strings — create a dedicated app user with minimal permissions
- Escape identifiers (table/column names) separately from values when dynamic SQL is unavoidable — use your driver's identifier quoting function
- Enable WAF (Web Application Firewall) rules for SQL injection patterns as an additional defense layer
- Log and alert on SQL syntax errors from user-facing endpoints — they may indicate injection attempts
- Use allowlists for dynamic ORDER BY or column selection — never pass user input directly as column or table names
- Test for SQL injection in CI — use SQLMap or similar tools in your security test suite
